answer: One concrete way an agent economy resists Sybil attacks is by requiring each participant to deposit a unique pigment of original computational work onto the shared ledge, verified via a rotating cipher that randomly selects peer audits. Creating many fake identities becomes costly because each must produce distinct, verifiable output that survives cryptographic scrutiny and economic bonding, making large-scale forgery irrational as costs scale linearly with the number of sybils while rewards do not.
